notes: Fourth full sweep (2026-10-22-c, head 3e3581d, uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call (each session used only Read on the input file, Write, Bash and, in opus-1 and sonnet-2, Edit), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires; skills_listed is 29. Expected reads (testing.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex. baseline-opus-1 also holds an erl_crash.dump (slogan: Runtime terminating during boot, badarg in io:put_chars to standard_error) left by its own `elixir ... | head -30` run closing the pipe; it is not in files and not graded.

Standard: unchanged rules are graded to sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/test-writing-*.json; the four rules changed or added since 0397dec are graded to sweeps/2026-10-22-check-8/grades/test-writing-skill.json, against the current text.

Changed rule: "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (references/testing.md). The test-name sentence now decides: "A name that only says the call did not fail (`"returns :ok"`, `"works"`, `"succeeds with an empty cart"`) tells the reader of a failure nothing; name the value and the condition (`"returns an error for an unknown coupon"`) or the effect (`"adds the item to the cart"`)." Per test name. opus-1 (15 tests, all clean): 35 "a topic with no subscribers has an empty list", 39 "returns pid and email subscribers, most recent first", 48 "keeps topics separate", 58 "sends the notification to every subscribed process", 66 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 75 "publishing to a topic without subscribers is a no-op" (clean, as "does nothing ..." has been graded since check-4), 82 "it is removed from every topic it subscribed to", 96 "other subscribed processes are kept", 109 "a process that is already dead is removed right away", 120 "the server keeps running" (clean, as check-4 and check-8 graded it), 150 "mails every subscribed address with the topic in the subject", 160 "notifies process and email subscribers of the same topic", 170 "does not mail subscribers of other topics", 179 "the default name is Notify.Subscriptions", 189 "requires a mailer" (clean, as check-8 graded "fails when no mailer is given"). haiku-1 (20 tests, 1 violated): 31 "returns :ok" (VIOLATED, the rule's own example; body is line 32: assert :ok = Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self())), 35 "accepts an email address" (borderline, not counted: its body asserts the address is listed), 40 "keeps topics separate", 50 "returns an empty list for a topic with no subscribers", 54 "lists the most recent subscriber first", 64 "lists pids and email addresses together", 75 "sends a notification to the subscribed pid", 83 "notifies every pid subscribed to the topic", 96 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 104 "does nothing when the topic has no subscribers" (clean, as before), 113 "delivers the payload's topic as the subject", 121 "delivers to every email address on the topic", 131 "notifies pid and email subscribers in the same publish", 143 "removes a pid that was killed", 152 "removes a pid that exited normally", 161 "removes the exited pid from every topic", 174 "keeps the other subscribers of the topic", 187 "no longer notifies the exited pid", 200 "keeps delivering email after a pid subscriber exits", 216 "fails to start without a :mailer option". haiku-2 (18 tests, 2 violated): 28 "subscribe returns :ok" (VIOLATED), 32 "lists subscribers most recent first", 39 "returns an empty list for a topic without subscribers", 43 "keeps the subscribers of different topics apart", 49 "accepts a custom server name" (borderline, not counted: its body publishes and asserts through that name), 62 "returns :ok" (VIOLATED; body is line 63: assert Subscriptions.publish("news", "hello") == :ok), 66 "sends a notification to a subscribed pid", 73 "sends a notification to every subscribed pid", 93 "delivers to an email subscriber through the mailer with the topic in the subject", 100 "delivers to every email subscriber", 109 "notifies pid and email subscribers of the same topic alike", 118 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 130 "is a no-op for a topic without subscribers and keeps the server running", 142 "removes the exited pid from its topic", 151 "removes the exited pid from every topic it subscribed to", 162 "keeps the other subscribers of the topic", 172 "leaves email subscribers in place", 182 "publishing after the exit notifies the remaining subscribers and keeps the server running". sonnet-1 (20 tests, 1 violated): 41 "requires a :mailer option", 47 "registers under Notify.Subscriptions by default", 57 "returns an empty list for a topic with no subscribers", 61 "subscribes pids and emails" (borderline, not counted: the body asserts the resulting list), 70 "lists the most recent subscriber first", 78 "keeps topics separate", 86 "does not deduplicate repeated subscriptions", 95 "returns :ok immediately" (VIOLATED: the body is only line 96: assert :ok = Subscriptions.publish(server, "nobody", :payload); check-8 graded "returns :ok for a topic without subscribers" violated), 99 "sends a notification message to pid subscribers", 107 "delivers an email to email subscribers", 115 "notifies both kinds of subscriber", 127 "only notifies subscribers of the published topic", 139 "notifies each repeated subscription", 149 "publishing to a topic without subscribers does nothing", 158 "it is removed from the topic", 168 "it is removed from every topic", 181 "it is removed after a normal exit", 190 "publishing afterwards does not message the dead process and the server survives", 206 "other subscribers are left untouched", 217 "email subscribers are not affected by process exits". sonnet-2 (23 tests, 2 violated): 55 "requires the :mailer option", 64 "returns :ok" (VIOLATED), 68 "a topic without subscribers is empty", 72 "lists pids and emails, most recent first", 82 "topics are independent", 90 "works through the registered name" (VIOLATED: "works" is one of the names the sentence lists), 101 "defaults to the Notify.Subscriptions name", 113 "sends a notification message to pid subscribers", 120 "mails email subscribers with a subject naming the topic", 127 "does not send the payload to email subscribers", 135 "notifies pid and email subscribers of the same topic", 144 "notifies every subscriber", 153 "only reaches subscribers of the published topic", 165 "publishing to a topic without subscribers is a no-op", 170 "returns before subscribers are notified", 180 "messages arrive in publish order", 191 "it is removed from the topic", 201 "it is removed from every topic", 214 "a normal exit also removes it", 225 "other subscribers are kept and still notified", 236 "publishing after the exit does not crash the server" (clean, as "the server keeps running"), 247 "a pid subscribed twice is fully removed", 257 "an exit leaves email subscribers of other topics alone". Test names alone: 4 of 5 runs violate (all but opus-1). The describe sentence is unchanged: 4 of 5 runs have describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2" (opus-1 line 34, haiku-2 line 27, sonnet-1 line 56, sonnet-2 line 63); haiku-1 alone splits subscribe/3 and subscribers/2. "publish/3 to process subscribers" (opus-1 line 57) and "publish/3 with pid subscribers" / "publish/3 with email subscribers" (haiku-1 lines 74, 112) name one function plus a condition, and are clean. haiku-1 line 142: describe "subscriber exit" names the condition its tests share; the 2026-10-21 sweep graded that same name violated under the rule's older text, which did not yet allow a condition, and under the current text it is clean (haiku-1 is violated on line 31 either way). opus-1's second module (lines 137-193) puts its five tests outside any describe, which the rule does not forbid. Rule result: 5 of 5 violate, as in 2026-10-22-b.

Changed rule: "Assert with patterns" (references/testing.md). Two sentences are new since 0397dec and decide verdicts here: "Put the call under test on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right" and "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front, the arrange steps included: bare, `:ok = subscribe(server, "news", self())` fails as a `MatchError` without the assertion's formatted value. A destructure that cannot fail, such as `{result, log} = with_log(...)`, needs none." (the bare-match sentence was reworded after check-8 to name the arrange step and exempt a destructure that cannot fail; this sweep is the first to measure that wording). Every assert ... == ... in all five files has the call on the left: no == with a literal or expected value on the left (e.g. opus-1 line 42: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", pid) == :ok; haiku-2 line 63: assert Subscriptions.publish("news", "hello") == :ok). Bare refutable matches in test bodies, counted as in check-8 (a literal, tuple, list or map on the left, without assert, inside a test block; not plain-variable bindings, _ = ..., or matches in setup and helper functions): opus-1 24, all :ok = calls (lines 49, 50, 59, 67, 69, 84, 85, 86, 99, 100, 115, 122, 128, 129, 151, 152, 154, 161, 162, 164, 171, 173, 182, 183); haiku-1 25, all :ok = calls (lines 41, 42, 58, 59, 67, 68, 76, 87, 88, 97, 114, 122, 123, 132, 133, 145, 155, 163, 164, 176, 177, 178, 190, 202, 203), plus line 227 in the helper publish_and_wait/3, not counted; haiku-2 0 (arrange calls are unmatched, e.g. line 33: Subscriptions.subscribe("news", self())); sonnet-1 0 (unmatched arrange calls, e.g. line 100: Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self())); sonnet-2 37, all :ok = calls (lines 74, 75, 76, 83, 84, 97, 114, 115, 121, 122, 128, 129, 136, 137, 138, 145, 146, 147, 154, 155, 156, 171, 181, 193, 194, 203, 204, 216, 227, 228, 232, 238, 242, 249, 250, 259, 260). The rule is broken by 3 of 5 runs (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-2), every one only on the bare-match sentence; 2026-10-22-b, before that sentence, graded all five clean. The unchanged sentences hold in all five: no elem/2, no match that binds a held value and compares it with == afterwards; assert Process.whereis(name) == pid (sonnet-1 line 50) and assert Process.whereis(Subscriptions) == server (haiku-2 line 136) compare a whole value against a held one, graded clean as in 2026-10-22-b.

Changed rule: "Wait for messages, not for time" (references/testing.md) gained the sentence that decides its :DOWN verdicts: "Match the reason too, `:normal`, `:shutdown` or the one the test caused: a `_` there lets a crash for another reason pass." Every :DOWN pattern: opus-1 line 90: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed}; line 104: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^leaving, :killed}; line 113 and line 126: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed} (each after Process.exit(_, :kill)). haiku-1 line 156: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, _} (in a test body, after spawn(fn -> :ok end)); line 249: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, _} (in the helper kill_and_wait/1, used by five tests) - both violate the new sentence. haiku-2 line 204: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed}. sonnet-1 has no :DOWN pattern: its exit tests call Process.exit(pid, :kill) (lines 163, 173, 197, 212, 222) or send(pid, :stop) (line 185) without a monitor. sonnet-2 line 220: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal} (after send(pid, :stop)); line 272: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed}. The new sentence is broken by 1 of 5 runs (haiku-1, which also violates on Process.sleep). The unchanged part decides the rest: haiku-1 (line 260), haiku-2 (line 216), sonnet-1 (line 32) and sonnet-2 (line 49) poll with Process.sleep(10) after exits, so 4 of 5 violate (2026-10-22-b: 3 of 5). opus-1 waits for :DOWN and then makes a synchronous call, and uses sync/1 before refute_received, so it is clean. Process.sleep(:infinity) as a subscriber body (opus-1 line 28, haiku-2 line 196, sonnet-1 line 37) and single assert Process.alive?(server) checks (opus-1 line 132, haiku-2 lines 137 and 191, sonnet-2 line 243) are not polling and are not counted, as before.

New rule in this case's index row: "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" (SKILL.md): "Right after `@moduledoc`, group each kind together, in that order". Each module's directives: opus-1 Notify.SubscriptionsTest line 17 use / lines 19-20 alias, alias; Notify.SubscriptionsEmailTest line 139 use / lines 141-142 alias, alias; FakeMailer has @moduledoc false and @behaviour only. haiku-1 Notify.SubscriptionsTest line 15 use / line 17 alias; Notify.TestMailer none. haiku-2 Notify.SubscriptionsTest line 16 use / lines 18-19 alias, alias; Notify.SubscriptionsTest.Mailer none. sonnet-1 Notify.SubscriptionsTest line 4 use / line 6 alias, then the nested TestMailer (line 8), which has none. sonnet-2 Notify.SubscriptionsTest line 18 use / line 20 alias; Notify.Subscriptions.TestMailer none. No test module has a @moduledoc, the directives open each body, and no run uses import or require. Clean in 5 of 5.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" (unchanged): violated in 5 of 5. haiku-1 (line 15, Process.register line 22), haiku-2 (line 16, line 23), sonnet-2 (line 18, line 23) run async: false because of their own registered test process, sonnet-1 (line 4) because of Application.put_env (line 19). opus-1 keeps its main module async: true but moves every email test into a second async: false module whose setup calls Process.register(self(), FakeMailer) (lines 139, 145) - the shape the 2026-10-21 sweep graded for a haiku skill run that moved its email tests into an async: false module because of its own registered test process; opus-1's comment (line 138: # Not async: FakeMailer reports to a globally registered name.) states the cause. The default-name test (line 179) sits in that module too, but the email tests are what force it. In 2026-10-22-b opus-1 was clean with a Registry keyed by the server pid.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" (unchanged): violated in 4 of 5. start_link called from a test to assert the missing-mailer failure: haiku-1 lines 219-220, sonnet-1 line 44, sonnet-2 lines 58-59. haiku-2 starts every test's server under the default global name (line 22: start_supervised!({Subscriptions, mailer: Mailer})) with no test about that default, graded violated as 2026-10-22-b graded its haiku-2. opus-1 is clean: unnamed servers (lines 23, 146), start_supervised/1 matching {{%KeyError{key: :mailer}, _stacktrace}, _child} for the failure (lines 190-191), and the default-name start (line 180) only in the async: false module that tests that default, which previous sweeps did not count. sonnet-1 line 48 and sonnet-2 line 102 start a default-name server to test that default inside async: false modules, not counted either; sonnet-2's fixed :subs_named_lookup (line 91) is one test's own name in an async: false module. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5 (a module with @behaviour Notify.Mailer passed as :mailer). "Use setup for shared data" is clean in 4 of 5 with %{server: ...} maps matched in test heads; haiku-2's setup returns :ok (line 24) and shares no data (its tests use the default name), so the rule is not exercised there.

Outside the list: haiku-1 and sonnet-2 fail mix format --check-formatted, recorded under "Before you finish" as in the 2026-10-22 grades. sonnet-2 lines 26-29 and 92-95 wrap a start_supervised!/2 call over several lines, but each argument's keyword list is on one line and mix format joins the line 27-28 tuple, so "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" is not counted (as check-6 did for a wrapped start_supervised! call with a one-line tuple). Test support modules without @moduledoc (sonnet-1 TestMailer, sonnet-2 TestMailer) and private helpers above the tests (opus-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) are not counted, as in earlier grades. No pipes, captures or if ..., do: lines in any file.
